anchors.0: The proposed capability is ordinary commodity software with no defensible operating advantage.
anchors.25: Differentiation is temporary or readily purchased by every competitor.
anchors.50: Some proprietary integration or process advantage is plausible but not established.
anchors.75: Owned workflow access, feedback and execution create a credible advantage over generic tools.
anchors.100: Evidence supports a hard-to-replicate operating capability rooted in lawful access, accumulated context, verification and execution.

evidence_expectations: Distinctiveness: Comparison against existing software/services and generic AI, access rights, operating feedback loops, integration depth and replication cost; no vague AI moat claims.
Seek and retain evidence against the favored interpretation; source absence is not proof of absence.
Return a numeric defensible estimate with rationale, reduced confidence/evidence quality, explicit alternatives and a gap; never call an unsupported estimate a fact.

Confidence guidance: {"0.25": "Weak assumption with little direct support", "0.5": "Mixed indirect support and unresolved alternatives", "0.75": "Several relevant consistent sources with limited unresolved alternatives", "0.95": "Strong representative and independently corroborated evidence"}. These are declared calibration anchors, not observed confidence statistics.

Evidence-quality guidance: {"0.25": "Sparse, indirect or strongly selected material", "0.5": "Relevant but partial, dated or unrepresentative material", "0.75": "Current directly relevant material with known limitations", "0.95": "Current representative and independently verified material"}. Evidence quality and confidence may overlap; report raw scores alongside adjusted scores.
Downside: 0–100 points, separately justified by a named adverse scenario and score impact; do not deduct risks already reflected in raw score or eligibility a second time.

Ownership economics must work without AI gains. A high AI judgment needs named inputs, persistent entities, triggers, authorized actions, verification, failure modes, human controls, measurable output and retained economics.

anchors.0: Customers/vendors capture the benefit or implementation costs exceed sustained gains.
anchors.25: Most gains are competed away, require constant reinvestment or depend on optimistic revenue conversion.
anchors.50: Some retained value is plausible but pricing, demand conversion and recurring costs are uncertain.
anchors.75: Owner plausibly retains material net earnings after deployment, review, ongoing operation and customer pass-through.
anchors.100: Evidence supports durable retained incremental cash earnings under explicit conservative costs, pricing and competitive responses.

evidence_expectations: Retained economic value: Mechanistic earnings bridge, utilization/revenue conversion, pricing/pass-through, software/model/integration/review costs and competitive response; avoid double-counting base earnings and task savings.
